e_en: A alone can complete 1/3rd of a work in 5 days A alone can complete the whole work in 5 × 3 = 15 days B can complete 2/5th of a work in 10 days B can complete the whole work in 10 × 5/2 = 25 days Total work = 75 work done by A and B in 6 days = (5 + 3) × 6 = 48 Remaining work = 75 – 48 = 27 Let efficiency of C be x, then 18x = 27 ⇒ x = 27/18 = 1.5 C alone can complete the whole work in = 75/1.5 = 50 days

q_en: The speed of a boat in still water is 15 km/h. The speed of the current is 3 km/h. In how much time (in hours) will the boat travel a distance of 54 km upstream and the same distance downstream?
e_en: Speed of boat = 15 km/h Speed of current = 3 km/h Speed of boat upstream = 15 – 3 = 12 km/h Speed of boat downstream = 15 + 3 = 18 km/h According to the question Required time to cover 54 km distance downstream and upstream = 54/18 + 54/12 = 7 hours 30 min

q_en: The total marks scored by Amit in English and S. Studies is what percent (correct to one decimal place) more than the marks scored by him in Maths?
e_en: Number of marks scored by Amit in English and S.Studies = 64 + 68 = 132 Number of marks scored by Amit in Maths = 80 Required percentage = (132 – 80)/80 × 100 = 65%

q_en: Three successive discounts of 20%, 20% and 30% are offered on an article. If the marked price of the article is Rs. 750, then what will be selling price?
e_en: Given: Marked price of the article = Rs. 750 Formula Used: SP = (1 – d1/100) x (1 – d2/100) x (1 – d3/100) x MP, where SP is the selling price and MP is the marked price. and d1, d2, d3 are the three successive discounts. Calculation: SP of the article after getting three successive discounts of 20%, 20% and 30% = 750 × (80/100) × (80/100) × (70/100) = Rs. 336 Hence, the correct answer is Rs. 336

q_en: The sum of the present ages of a father and his son is 78 years. After five years, the ratio of their ages becomes 7 : 4. What is the present age (in years) of the father?
e_en: Sum of the present ages of son and father is = 78 years Sum of the ages of son and father after 5 years = 78 + 10 = 88 5 years after the ratio of father and son = 7x : 4x According to the question 7x + 4x = 88 ⇒ 11x = 88 ⇒ x = 88/11 ⇒ x = 8 5 years after the age of father = 7 × 8 = 56 Present age of father = 56 – 5 = 51

q_en: Three positive numbers are in the proportion of 3 : 4 : 6. If the sum of their squares is 244, then what is the largest number?
e_en: The ratio of three numbers are = 3x : 4x : 6x According to the question (3x)² + (4x)² + (6x)² = 244 ⇒ 9x² + 16x² + 36x² = 244 ⇒ 61x² = 244 ⇒ x² = 244/61 ⇒ x² = 4 ⇒ x = √4 ⇒ x = 2 The largest number is = 6 × 2 = 12

q_en: A man travels from P to Q at the speed of 60 km/h and travels from Q to P at the speed of 90 km/h. What is the average speed of the man for the whole journey?
e_en: Short trick: Average speed = (2 × 60 × 90)/(60 + 90) = 72 km/hr Detailed Solution: As we know, Average speed = Total distance/total time Let the distance between P and Q be x km, then Average speed = 2x/[x/60 + x/90] = 2x/[(3x + 2x)/180] = (2x × 180)/5x = 72 km/hr

q_en: A bag contains one rupee, 50 paise and 25 paise coins in the proportion 5 : 7 : 9. If the total amount in the bag is Rs. 430, then how many 25 paise coins are there?
e_en: Ratio of coins of Rs. 1, 50 paise and 25 paise in the bag = 5 : 7 : 9 Ratio of value (price) of Rs. 1, 50 paise and 25 paise = 5/1 : 7/2 : 9/4 = 20 : 14 : 9 Ratio of value (price) of Rs. 1, 50 paise and 25 paise = 20x : 14x : 9x According to the question 20x + 14x + 9x = 430 ⇒ 43x = 430 ⇒ x = 430/43 ⇒ x = 10 Price of 25 paise in the bag = 9 × 10 = Rs. 90 Coins of 25 paise in the bag = 90 × 4 = 360

q_en: A train crosses two platforms of length 1000 m and 600 m in 80 seconds and 60 seconds respectively. What is the length of the train?
e_en: Let the length of the train be x m. As we know, Speed = (x + 1000)/80 ---(1) Speed = (x + 600)/60 ---(2) From equation (1) and equation (2) (x + 1000)/80 = (x + 600)/60 ⇒ 3 (x + 1000) = 4 (x + 600) ⇒ 3x + 3000 = 4x + 2400 ⇒ 4x – 3x = 3000 – 2400 ⇒ x = 600 Length of the train is 600 m.

q_en: Rs. 20000 is invested on compound interest (compounded half-yearly) at the rate of 20% per annum, then what will be the interest after two years?
e_en: Given: ​P = 2000 t = 2 years r = 20% Concept used: Amount = P[1 + (R/100)]T When compounded half-yearly, T = 2 × T R = R/2 CI = A - P Calculation: If interest compounded half-yearly, then T= 2 × 2 = 4 R = 20/2 = 10% A = 20000 × (11/10) × (11/10) × (11/10) × (11/10) ⇒ A = 29282 CI = 29282 – 20000 ⇒ CI = Rs. 9282 ∴ CI is Rs 9282. 9b

q_en: The length and the breadth of a rectangle are 15 cm and 12 cm respectively. If the rectangle is given one full rotation about its breadth as the axis, what is the volume (in cm³) through which the rectangle moves?
e_en: Given: Length of rectangle = 15 cm Breadth of rectangle = 12 cm Formula used: Volume of cylinder = πr2h Calculation: Radius of the cylinder = 15 cm [length of the rectangle] Height of the cylinder = 12 cm [breadth of the rectangle] As we know, Volume of the cylinder = πr²h Volume of the cylinder = π × 15 × 15 × 12 = 2700π ∴ Volume of cylinder is 2700π cm³

q_en: The cost price of an article is 6/7 of its selling price. What will be the profit or loss percentage?
e_en: Let the selling price of the article be Rs. 7 Cost price of the article = 7 × (6/7) = Rs. 6 Profit = 7 – 6 = 1 Profit percentage = (1/6) × 100 = 16.67%

q_en: What is the average of the first 15 even numbers starting from 2?
e_en: Short Trick- 1 Average of first n even number = (n + 1) Average of first 15 even numbers = 15 + 1 = 16 Short Trick- 2 As we know, Average of any AP median of that series. Median of series = [(15 + 1)/2]th = 8th term So, the 8th term of series is 16. Detailed Solution : As we know, Sum of first n even numbers = n (n + 1) Sum of first 15 even numbers = 15 × 16 = 240 Average of first 15 even numbers = 240/15 = 16.

q_en: 30 kg of rice costing Rs. 50 per kg is mixed with 20 kg of rice costing Rs. 60 per kg. What is the average cost of the mixture per kg?
e_en: Cost of 30 kg rice costing Rs. 50 per kg = 50 × 30 = Rs. 1500 Cost of 20 kg rice costing Rs. 60 per kg = 60 × 20 = Rs. 1200 Total cost of 50 kg mixed rice = 1500 + 1200 = Rs. 2700 Cost of 1 kg mixed rice = 2700/50 = Rs. 54

q_en: The profit earned on an article is 25% when it is calculated on the cost price. If the profit is calculated on the selling price, then what will be the profit percentage?
e_en: Given: Profit is 25% when calculated on CP Formula Used: Profit = SP – CP, Profit % when calculated on CP, ⇒ Profit /CP × 100 Profit % when calculated on SP, ⇒ Profit /SP × 100, Where, CP is cost price, SP is selling price Calculation: Let the cost price be Rs. 100 Profit % when calculated on CP, ⇒ 25 = Profit/100 × 100 ⇒ 25 = Profit Profit = SP – CP ⇒ SP = 100 + 25 ⇒ SP = Rs.

q_en: Manish’s salary is half of Ravi’s salary. Ravi’s salary is how much percentage more than Manish’s Salary?
e_en: Let salary of Ravi be Rs. 100 Salary of Manish = 100 × (1/2) = Rs. 50 Ravi salary is more than that of Manish by = 100 – 50 = 50 Ravi salary is more than that of Manish by (in%) = (50/50) × 100 = 100%

q_en: A sum of Rs. 800 invested on simple interest becomes Rs. 1200 in 8 years. What will be simple interest for 6 years on the sum at the same rate of interest?
e_en: Short Trick: SI for 8 years = 1200 – 800 = 400 SI for 6 years = 400 × (6/8) = 300 Detailed Method: P = 800, A = 1200 and t = 8 years ⇒ SI = 1200 – 800 = 400 As we know, SI = Prt/100 400 = (800 × r × 8)/100 ⇒ r = (400 × 100)/(800 × 8) ⇒ r = 25/4 % Again, If time = 6 years, then SI = (800 × 25 × 6)/(100 × 4) ⇒ SI = 300

q_en: What is the area of the largest circle which can be inscribed in a square of side 28 cm?(Take π = 22/7)
e_en: Given: Side of the square = 28 cm If a circle is inscribed in the square, then Diameter of the circle is = side of the square = 28 cm Radius of the circle = 28/2 = 14 cm Area of the circle = πr² = (22/7) × 14 × 14 = 616 cm²

q_en: What is the difference in the number of refrigerators supplied to the hotel by companies C1 and C5 if the total number of refrigerators is 3700?
e_en: The difference in percentage of refrigerators supplied to the hotel by companies C1 and C5 is = 26% - 21% = 5% As we know, When 5 is multiplied by any number the unit digit will be 0 or 5. So, 185 is the correct option. If total number of refrigerator is 3700, then The difference in percentage of refrigerators supplied to the hotel by companies C1 and C5 is = 3700 × [(26 - 21)/100] = 185 ∴ The required difference is 185.

q_en: If the total number of refrigerators in the hotel is 3700, then what is the number of refrigerators of company C5?

q_en: What is the difference between the central angles (to the nearest 0.1 degree) subtended by the sectors for C2 and C4?

q_en: A rectangular paper of width 7 cm is rolled along its length and a cylinder of radius 9 cm is formed. The volume of the cylinder is:(Take π = 22/7)

q_en: If the difference between the simple and compound interests on a sum of money for 2 years at 5% p.a. is Rs. 125, the sum (in Rs.) is:
e_en: As we know, Percentage Difference in two years of CI and SI = P(r/100)² % ⇒ 125 = (P × 5 × 5)/(100 × 100) ⇒ P = (125 × 100 × 100)/(5 × 5) ∴ P = 50000

q_en: The radii of two cylinders A and B are in the ratio of 5 : 6 and the heights are in the ratio of 7 : 4 respectively. The ratio of curved surface area of cylinder B to that of A is:
e_en: As we know, Curved surface area of cylinder = 2πrh The ratio of radius of two cylinder A and B (r₁ : r₂) = 5 : 6 The ratio of height of two cylinder A and B (h₁ : h₂) = 7 : 4 ∴ The ratio of curved surface area of cylinder B and A = (2πr₂h₂) : (2πr₁h₁) = (6 × 4) : (5 × 7) = 24 : 35

q_en: A shopkeeper purchased 120 pears for Rs. 15 each. However, 10 pears were rotten and thrown away. The remaining sold at Rs. 18 each. What will be the percentage profit?
e_en: Cost of 1 pear = Rs. 15 Cost of 120 pears = 120 × 15 = Rs. 1800 SP of 1 pear = Rs. 18 SP of 120 pears = 110 × 18 = Rs. 1980 Hence, Profit = 1980 – 1800 = 180 ∴ Profit percentage = (180/1800) × 100 = 10%

q_en: If LCM of two numbers 390 and 420 is 5460, then the HCF of two numbers is:
e_en: As we know Multiplication of two numbers = HCF × LCM ⇒ HCF × 5460 = 390 × 420 ⇒ HCF = (390 × 420)/5460 ⇒ HCF = 30

q_en: In a school there are 550 students. The ratio of the boys to that of the girls is 6 : 5. How many more girls should join the school so that the ratio becomes 5 : 6?
e_en: Total number of students in the school = 550 Number of girls in the school = 550 × (5/11) = 250 Number of boys in the school = 550 – 250 = 300 Let the x girls join the school. 300/(250 + x) = 5/6 ⇒ 6/5 × 300 = 250 + x ⇒ x = 360 – 250 ∴ x = 110

q_en: At the rate of 8% the amount invested earns a simple interest of Rs. 240 after 3 years. If the rate of interest been 5% more, then how much more interest would it have earned?
e_en: Short Trick: SI on rate 8% = Rs. 240 SI on Rate 5% = [240/8] × 5 = Rs. 150 Detailed Method: SI = 240, r = 8% and time = 3 years As we know, SI = P × r × t/100 ⇒ 240 = (P × 8 × 3)/100 ⇒ P = (240 × 100)/24 ⇒ P = 1000 Again, New rate = 8% + 5% = 13% P = 1000, and time = 3 years SI = (1000 × 13 × 3)/100 ⇒ SI = 390 ∴ The interest more than that of before = 390 – 240 = 150.

q_en: Two pipes P and Q can fill an empty tank in 20 min and 10 min respectively. R can empty a full tank in 15 minutes. If all three pipes are opened together, how much time (in minutes) will they take to fill the tank?
e_en: Let capacity of tank = LCM of (20, 10 and 15) = 60 units Hence, efficiency of P = 60/20 = 3 units/min Efficiency of Q = 60/10 = 6 units/min Efficiency of R = - 60/15 = - 4 units/min Now, combined efficiency = 3 + 6 – 4 = 5 units/min ∴ Time taken = 60/5 = 12 minutes

q_en: In an examination, there are 800 boys and 600 girls. 40% boys and 60% girls passed the examination. The percentage (correct to two decimal places) of failed students from the total students is:
e_en: Number of boys = 800 Number of girls = 600 Hence, total students = 800 + 600 = 1400 Number of boys who failed = 800 × (60/100) = 480 Number of girls who failed = 600 × (40/100) = 240 Hence, total failed students = 480 + 240 = 720 ∴ The percentage of failed students = (720/1400) × 100 = 51.43%

q_en: Kartik’s father age is four times the age of Kartik. Three years ago, Kartik’s father age was seven times the age of Kartik. The present age of Kartik is:
e_en: Let the age of kartik be x, then The age of kartik’s father = 4x According to the question (x – 3)/(4x – 3) = 1/7 ⇒ 7 (x – 3) = 4x – 3 ⇒ 7x – 21 = 4x – 3 ⇒ 7x – 4x = 21 – 3 ⇒ 3x = 18 ⇒ x = 18/3 ∴ x = 6

q_en: The diagonal of a square is equal to the side of an equilateral triangle. If the area of the square is 18√3 sq. cm. What is the area (in cm²) of the equilateral triangle?
e_en: As we know, Area of the equilateral triangle = [√3/4] a² Diagonal of a square = √2 a Area of the square = a² a² = 18√3 ⇒ a = √[18 √3] Diagonal of a square = √2a Diagonal of the square = √2 × √[18 √3] Side of the equilateral triangle = √2 × √[18 √3] [Diagonal of the square] Area of the equilateral triangle = [√3/4] [√2 × √(18 √3)]² = [√3/4] × 2 × (18 √3) = 27

q_en: If a student walks with speed 30% more than the usual speed, he reaches 15 min earlier to his destination. How much time (in minutes) does he take to reach his destination normally?
e_en: 30% = 3/10 Let the normal speed of the student be 10x Hence, increased speed of the students = 10x × (13/10) = 13x Ratio of speed of student normally to increased = 10x : 13x Hence, time ratio taken by student normally to after = 13x : 10x As we know, Time is inversely proportional to speed. 13x – 10x = 15 min ⇒ 3x = 15 ⇒ x = 15/3 = 5 min ∴ Normal time = 13 × 5 = 65 min

q_en: A man starts off a journey. He travelled for 16 hours in total. First half of the distance was covered at 40 km/h and the second half at 60 km/h. What was the distance covered?

q_en: What is the sum of the digits of the largest six-digit number divisible by 3, 4, 5 and 6?

q_en: How much time will it take a principal of Rs. 640 to yield Rs. 768 as an amount at 2.5% simple interest per annum?

q_en: The ratio between the volume (in cm³) and the curved surface area (in cm²) of a cylinder is numerically 14 : 1. If the height of the cylinder is 50 cm, then what is the volume of the cylinder? (Take π = 22/7)
e_en: As we know, Volume of the cylinder = πr²h Curved surface area of the cylinder = 2πrh Height of the cylinder (h) = 50 cm According to the question πr²h/2πrh = 14/1 ⇒ r/2 = 14 ⇒ r = 14 × 2 ⇒ r = 28 cm Volume of the cylinder = πr²h = (22/7) × 28 × 28 × 50 = 123200 cm³ ∴ The correct answer is 123200 cm³.

q_en: 6 pencils cost Rs. 30 and 12 pens cost Rs. 120. What is the average cost of 50 pencils and 50 pens?

q_en: A family consists of two grandparents, two parents and four children. Two years ago, the average age of the grandparents was 72 years. One year ago, the average age of parents was 36 years. At present, the average age of the children is 12 years. What is the present average age of the family?

q_en: A, B and C can alone do a task in 40, 120 and 36 days, respectively. A and B together work for 20 days and leave the task incomplete. C resumes it and complete it alone. How many days did C take to complete it?
e_en: Total work = 360 Work done by A and B in 20 days = (9 + 3) × 20 = 240 Remaining work, C will complete in = (360 - 240)/10 = 12 days

q_en: A company bought a machine for Rs. 40000 and spent Rs. 10000 on its repair. After some time, the machine was sold for Rs. 45000. How much discount was offered?
e_en: Cost of machine for company = 40,000 Company spent on machine = Rs. 10,000 Final cost of machine = Rs. 40,000 + Rs. 10,000 = Rs. 50,000 Company sold the machine = Rs. 45,000 Discount = Rs. 50,000 - Rs. 45,000 = Rs. 5,000 Discount percentage = (5,000/50,000) × 100 = 10%

q_en: A and B can together complete a task in 21 days. If A alone takes 42 days to complete the task, the number of days that B would take to do the task alone is:
e_en: A alone can complete the task in = 42 days A and B alone can complete the take in = 21 days Let B alone can complete the task in x days, According to the question 1/42 + 1/x = 1/21 ⇒ x = 1/21 - 1/42 ⇒ x = (2 - 1)/42 ⇒ x = 1/42 So, B alone can complete the whole task in 42 days. If remainder in each case is 1 and the number divisible by 13, then The number is (360x + 1) divisible by 13, so (360x + 1)/13 ⇒ 27x + (9x + 1)/13 (9x + 1) is divisible by 13 if we put x = 1, 2, 3, 4, …….. Put x = 10, then ⇒ (9 × 10 + 1) ⇒ 91 As we know, 91 is divisible by 13 so put x = 10 360x + 1 ⇒ 360 × 10 + 1 ⇒ 3600 + 1 ⇒ 3601 If 3601 is divisible by 31, the the remainder will be 5.

q_en: A hemisphere of radius 30 cm is moulded to form a cylinder of height 180 cm. The diameter of the cylinder is:
e_en: As we know Volume of hemisphere = (2/3) πr³ Volume of cylinder = πR²h Radius of hemisphere r = 30 cm Height of the cylinder h = 180 cm According to the question πR²h = (2/3) πr³ ⇒ R² × 180 = (2/3) × 30 × 30 × 30 ⇒ R² = (2 × 30 × 30 × 30)/(3 × 180) ⇒ R² = 100 ⇒ R = √100 ⇒ R = 10 cm Diameter of the cylinder = 2 × 10 = 20 cm

q_en: What is the total surface area of a cone which has a radius of 21 cm and a height of 28 cm? (Take π = 22/7)
e_en: Correct answer: 3696 cm².

q_en: In a mixture of 100 litres of milk and water, the ratio of milk and water is 3 : 2. If this ratio is to be 1 : 1, how much more water is to be added to the mixture?
e_en: Total quantity of mixture = 100 litres Ratio of milk and water = 3 : 2 Quantity of milk in the mixture = (3/5) × 100 = 60 Quantity of water in the mixture = 100 - 60 = 40 Let the quantity of water add in the mixture be x litres.

q_en: The price of a machine got depreciated by 50% in the 1st year, 33 1/3% in the 2ⁿd year and 25% in the 3rd year. Overall, by how much has the machine depreciated?
e_en: 50% = 1/2, 33 1/3% = 1/3 and 25% = 1/4 Let the price of the machine be Rs. x, then Price after depreciating = x × (1/2) × (2/3) × (3/4) = x/4 Price depreciating by = x - x/4 = 3x/4 Price depreciating by (in %) = [(3x/4)/x] × 100 = 75% Short trick: Price depreciating by (in %) = [(4 - 1)/4] × 100 = 75%

q_en: A train’s average speed is 72 km/h but is reduced to 60 km/h due to stoppages. For how much time does the train stop in an hour?
e_en: Without stoppage average speed = 72 km/h With stoppages average speed = 60 km/h As we know, Time of rest per hour equal to the difference in average speed divided by the speed without stoppage. Required time = [(72 - 60)/72] × 60 = 10 So, A train stops on an average 10 minute/hr

q_en: X did a task for 24 days and left in incomplete. He could have finished the task all by himself in a total of 36 days. Y, who can finish the task alone in 18 days, will take how many more days to complete the task?
e_en: Total work = 36 Work done by X in 24 days = 1 × 24 = 24 Remaining work = 36 - 24 = 12 Remaining work, Y complete in = 12/2 = 6 days.

q_en: A, B and C can complete a work alone in 400, 600 and 900 days respectively. In how many days can the work be completed if it is started by A and he is assisted by B and C on every second and third day respectively?
e_en: Given that, A, B and C can complete a work alone in 400, 600 and 900 days respectively, LCM of 400, 600 and 900 will be 3600. A’s one day work = 9 units B’s one day work = 6 units C’s one day work = 4 units A : (A + B) : (A + C) = 9 : 9 + 6 : 9 + 4 ⇒ 9 : 15 : 13 = 37 units 3 days = 37 units The will be completed in 3600/37 × 3 = 291.90 ∼ 292 days Note: The solution has been modified.

q_en:
A set of data is given: 4, 2, 3, 2, 7, 4, 8, 5, 2, 4, 5, 6, 2, 5, 6, 6, 5, 4, 6, 5, 3, 5, 4, 3
What is the mode of the set?
e_en: 4, 2, 3, 2, 7, 4, 8, 5, 2, 4, 5, 6, 2, 5, 6, 6, 5, 4, 6, 5, 3, 5, 4, 3 As we know, Mode = Maximum frequency Mode = 5 [because 5 has the maximum frequency 6 times]

q_en: What is the effective annual rate of interest corresponding to a rate of 10% per annum compounded half-yearly?
e_en: Rate of interest = 10% If interest compounded half-yearly = 10/2 = 5% Effective interest rate = 5% + 5% + [(5% × 5%)/100] = 10% + 0.25% = 10.25%

q_en: X took a loan of Rs. 5000 on simple interest, the rate of interest is the same as the number of years for which the loan was taken. If the interest paid was Rs. 1800, then what was the rate of interest?
e_en: Let the rate of interest be r% Time = r [Because time and rate in equal] P = 5000 and SI = 1800 As we know, SI = Prt/100 ⇒ 1800 = (5000 × r × r)/100 ⇒ r² = 1800/50 = 36 ⇒ r = √36 ⇒ r = 6 So, the rate of interest is 6%.

q_en: The number of students studying subjects A, B and C in a school is in the proportion of 12 : 15 : 16. There is a proposal to increase the number of students studying A, B and C, respectively by 50%, 20% and 50%. What will be the new proportion of the number of students studying A, B and C?
e_en: The ratio of number of subjects A, B and C = 12 : 15 : 16 The ratio of number of subjects after increment = 12 × (3/2) : 15 × (6/5) : 16 × (3/2) The ratio of number of subjects after increment = 18 : 18 : 24 or 3 : 3 : 4

q_en: What is the highest number which when divides the numbers 1026, 2052 and 4102, leaving remainders 2, 4 and 6 respectively?
e_en: The highest number which when divides the numbers 1026, 2052 and 4102, leaving remainders 2, 4 and 6 respectively, then ⇒ 1026 - 2 = 1024 ⇒ 2052 - 4 = 2048 ⇒ 4102 - 6 = 4096 HCF of 1024, 2048 and 4096 is 1024

q_en: Two trains are moving in opposite directions with speeds of 35 m/s and 45 m/s respectively. From the time they are 12 km apart, how much time would they take to cross each other?
e_en: Two trains are moving in opposite directions with speeds of 35 m/s and 45 m/s respectively. If the trains are running in the opposite direction, then Effective speed = 35 + 45 = 80 m/s Distance = 12 km or 12000 m As we know- Time = Distance/Speed Time = 12000/80 = 150 sec As we know 150 second = 2 min 30 sec

q_en: A customer was offered a discount of 40% on a piece of cloth. On insisting further, the shopkeeper agreed to a further discount of 20% on above. What was the effective discount offered to the customer?
e_en: Short Trick: Effective discount = 40 + 20 - [(40 × 20)/100] = 60 - 8 = 52% Detailed solution Let the marked price of the article be Rs. 100 Price of the article after discount = 100 × (60/100) × (80/100) = 48 Effective discount = 100 - 48 = 52 Effective discount (in %) = 52/100 × 100 = 52%

q_en: The value of 8 of 3 ÷ 6 + (10 + 2) × 3 - 96 ÷ 3 is:
The numbers are respectively 80% and 35% greater than a third number. What is the ratio of the two numbers?
e_en: Let the third number be 100 First number = 100 × 180/100 = 180 Second number = 100 × 135/100 = 135 Ratio of first to second number = 180 : 135 = 4 : 3

q_en: A boat travels upstream at the speed of 20 km/h and downstream at the speed of 30 km/h. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
e_en: Short trick: Speed of boat in still water = (30 + 20)/2 = 25 Detailed Method : Let the speed of boat be x km/hr and speed of the stream be y km/hr According to the question x + y = 30 ---(1) x – Y = 20 --- (2) From equation (1) and equation (2) ⇒ x = 25 Speed of boat in still water is 25 km/hr

q_en: If the height of a right circular cylinder is 10 cm and the curved surface area is 440 cm², then what is its radius?
e_en: Height of the cylinder h = 10 cm and radius of the cylinder = r cm. Curved surface area of the cylinder = 2πrh 2 πrh = 440 ⇒ 2 × 22/7 × r × 10 = 440 ⇒ r = 7 cm Radius of the cylinder is 7 cm.

q_en: The volume of a sphere and a right circular cylinder are the same. The radii of the sphere and the cylinder are 21 cm and 14 cm respectively. How much is the height of the cylinder?
e_en: Radius of sphere and cylinder are 21 and 14 cm respectively. As we know Volume of sphere = (4/3) πr³ Volume of cylinder = πr²h According to the question ⇒ π × 14 × 14 × h = (4/3) π × 21 × 21 × 21 ⇒ h = (4 × 21 × 21 × 21)/(3 × 14 × 14) ⇒ h = 63 cm

q_en: A man bought a shirt for Rs. 1000 and a pair of trousers for Rs. 2000. The discount offered on the shirt and the trousers were 20% and 50% respectively. What was the overall discount offered?
e_en: Marked price of shirt = 1000 × 100/80 = Rs. 1250 Marked price of trousers = 2000 × 100/50 = Rs. 4000 Total selling price of shirt and trousers = 1000 + 2000 = 3000 Total marked price of shirt and trousers = 1250 + 4000 = 5250 Total discount = 5250 - 3000 = 2250 ∴ Discount percentage = 2250 × 100/5250 = 900/21 = 42.85 ≈ 43%

q_en: A train travels 50% faster than a car. Both start at the same point and meet after travelling 360 km. In between, the train stopped for 2 hours at a station due to engine failure. What is the speed of the train?
e_en: Correct answer: 90 km/h.

q_en: A number is divided into three parts such that thrice the first part, six times the second part and eight times the third part are equal. If the first part is Rs. 1600, what is the third part?
e_en: Let the number divide by x, y and z, then ⇒ 3x = 6y = 8z Let 3x = 6y = 8z = k ⇒ 3x = k ⇒ x = k/3 Similarly, ⇒ 6y = k ⇒ y = k/6 and ⇒ 8z = k ⇒ z = k/8 Ratio of x : y : z = k/3 : k/6 : k/8 = 24/3 : 24/6 : 24/8 = 8 : 4 : 3 ⇒ 8 unit = 1600 ⇒ 1 unit = 200 ⇒ 3 unit = 600 Short Trick: If 3x = 6y = 8z, then x : y : z = 1/3 : 1/6 : 1/8 = 8 : 4 : 3 ⇒ 8 unit = 1600 ⇒ 1 unit = 200 ⇒ 3 unit = 600

q_en: An art exhibition was held during November month. The average number of visitors on weekdays and weekends(Saturday and Sunday) was 750 and 450 respectively. What was the average number of visitors for the month if the first day of the month was a Monday?
e_en: Given: The average number of visitors on weekdays and weekends were 750 and 450 Formula used: Average = sum of all observation/number of observation Calculation: Number of weekends (Saturday and Sunday) in the month = 8 (if the first day of th

q_en: A principal amount increases by 50% in five years at simple interest. At the same rate of interest, what will be the compound interest on Rs. 20000 for three years?
e_en: Simple interest for 5 years = 50% Simple interest for 1 year = 50/5 = 10% R = 10%, t = 3 years and P = 20000 As we know, A = P (1 + r/100)t ⇒ A = 20000 (1 + 10/100)³ ⇒ A = 20000 × 11/10 × 11/10 × 11/10 ⇒ A = 26620 ⇒ CI = 26620 – 20000 = 6620

q_en: Two bikes cost Rs. 40000 each. One of them is sold for Rs. 48000. At what price should the other be sold to get an overall profit of 25%?
e_en: Cost of bike = 40,000 Total cost price of both bikes = 40,000 × 2 = 80,000 Total profit = 80,000 × 25/100 = 20,000 Profit on first bike = 48,000 – 40,000 = 8,000 Profit on second bike should be = 20,000 – 8,000 = 12,000 Selling price of the second bike = 40,000 + 12,000 = 52,000

q_en: 30 dozen of nuts were bought for Rs. 14400 and another 32 packets of nuts (20 nuts in each packet) were bought for Rs. 57600. If the nuts are mixed and then sold in a packet of five for Rs. 432, then how much is the profit percentage?
e_en: Given: CP of 30 dozen of nuts = Rs. 14400 CP of 360 nuts = Rs. 14400 CP of 32 packets of nuts (20 nuts in each) = Rs. 57600 CP of 640 nuts = Rs. 57600 Calculation: Total nuts = 360 + 640 = 1000 Total CP = 14400 + 57600 = Rs. 72000 So CP of 1 nut = 72000/1000 = 72 CP of 5 nuts = 360 And SP of 5 nuts = 432 Profit = 432 - 360 = 72 ∴ Profit percentage = 72 × 100/360 = 20%

q_en: An examination was held on five subjects where the maximum marks for each subject was 100. X scored 82, 97, 88 and 91 in four subjects. If his aggregate was 90%, how much did he score in the fifth subject?
e_en: Let X scored in fifth subject be x, then Maximum score of five subject = 500 X score in five subject = 500 × 90/100 = 450 ⇒ 82 + 97 + 88 + 91 + x = 450 ⇒ x = 450 – 82 – 97 – 88 – 91 ⇒ x = 92

q_en: What is the mean of the first 20 whole numbers?
e_en: Concept used: Whole Numbers:- All natural numbers along with 0 is termed as the whole number Ex:- 0, 1, 2, 3, … , etc are all whole number 0 is the smallest whole number Every natural number is a whole number but every whole number is not a natural number. Calculation: Sum of first n natural number = n (n + 1)/2 Sum of first 19 natural number = (19 × 20)/2 = 190 Average of first 20 whole numbers = 190/20 = 9.5 As we know, Whole numbers = 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5…………..

q_en: The difference between two numbers is 15 and their HCF and LCM are 3 and 108 respectively. Find the difference between their reciprocals.
e_en: Let the two numbers are x and y ⇒ x – y = 15 and xy = 3 × 108 [Product of two number = HCF × LCM] ⇒ 1/y – 1/x ⇒ (x – y)/xy ⇒ 15/(3 × 108) ⇒ 5/108

q_en: A bike owner buys petrol at Rs. 64, Rs. 80 and Rs. 320 per litre for three consecutive years. What is the average cost per litre of petrol if he spends Rs. 32000 each year?
e_en: Number of litres consume of first year = 32000/64 = 500 litres Number of litres consume of second year = 32000/80 = 400 litres Number of litres consume of third year = 32000/320 = 100 litres Total consume petrol in three years = 500 + 400 + 100 = 1000 litres Total expenditure on petrol in three years = 32000 × 3 Average cost per litres of petrol = (32000 × 3)/1000 = Rs. 96

q_en: A, B and C can do a work in 16 days, while A and B can do the work in 40 days. In how many days can C do the work alone?
e_en: Total work = 80 Efficiency of C = 5 – 2 = 3 Work done by C alone in = 80/3 = 26.67 days

q_en: A can do a task alone in 96 days. B is thrice as efficient as A. A worked for 24 days alone and then B joined him. In how many days will they complete the remaining task together?
e_en: Let the efficiency of A be 1 unit Efficiency of B = 3 unit Total work = 96 Work done by A in 24 days = 24 Remaining work = 96 – 24 = 72 Remaining work, A and B complete in = 72/(1 + 3) = 72/4 = 18 days

q_en: The simple interest on a sum for five years at 7% per annum is Rs. 700. What is the principal amount?
e_en: SI = 700, t = 5 years and r = 7% As we know, SI = Prt/100 ⇒ 700 = (P × 7 × 5)/100 ⇒ P = 2000 Short Trick: Let the principal be 100% Rate for 1 year = 7% Rate for 5 years = 35% ⇒ 35% = 700 ⇒ 1% = 20 ⇒ 100% = 2000

q_en: The total number of articles sold by seller C to Shopkeeper Q is what percent of the total number of articles sold by seller F to the shopkeeper P?
e_en: Number of articles sold by seller C to shopkeeper Q is = 49 Number of articles sold by seller F to shopkeeper P is = 55 Required percentage = 49/55 × 100 = 89.09%

q_en: What is the average number of articles sold to shopkeeper P by the sellers A, B, C and D together?
e_en: Number of articles sold to shopkeeper P by the sellers A, B, C and D = 45 + 53 + 28 + 38 = 164 Required average = 164/4 = 41

q_en: What is the difference between total articles sold to P and Q by all the sellers other than A, B, C, D, E and F?
e_en: Articles sold to P by all the sellers other than A, B, C, D, E and F = 300 – (45 + 53 + 28 + 38 + 35 + 55) = 300 – 254 = 46 Articles sold to Q by all the sellers other than A, B, C, D, E and F = 500 – (56 + 49 + 49 + 38 + 65 + 60) = 500 – 317 = 183 Required difference = 183 – 46 = 137

q_en: A man goes to a place on the car at a speed of 160 km/h and comes back at a lower speed. If the average speed is 64km/h in total, then return speed (in km/h) is:
e_en: Let return speed of man be x, Average speed = 64 km/hr As we know, Average speed = 2xy/(x + y) ⇒ 64 = (2 × 160 × x)/(160 + x) ⇒ 160 + x = 320x/64 ⇒ 160 + x = 5x ⇒ 4x = 160 ⇒ x = 160/4 ⇒ x = 40 km/hr

q_en: Let ΔABD be on the same base AB and between the same parallels AB and CD. Then the relation between areas of ΔABC and ΔABD will be:
e_en: Given: The base of both triangles is the same and lies between the same parallel lines Concept used: Area of triangle = (1/2) × base × height Calculation: Here, Bases "AB" for both the triangle is the same Also, the height ( perpendicular distance between the parallel line) of both triangles will be the same (both triangles are between the same parallel lines) ∴ Area (ΔABC) = Area (ΔABD).

q_en: What is the difference between 0.9 and 0.9%?
e_en: As we know, ⇒ 0.9% = 0.9/100 = 0.009 Difference between 0.9 and 0.009 = 0.891

q_en: The ratio of cost price and selling price of an article is c : d. If d is 150% of c then the profit percentage on cost price is:
e_en: Given: The ratio of cost price and selling price of an article is c : d. d is 150% of c Formula: Profit% = (Selling price - Cost price)/Cost price × 100 Calculation: Let c be Rs. 100 ⇒ d = 100 × 150/100 = Rs. 150 Profit = 150 – 100 = 50 Profit % = 50/100 × 100 = 50% ∴ profit% = 50%&l

A contractor takes a contract to complete a road in 60 days and employed 105 labours. After 25 days, he found that one-third of the work is completed. How many more labours he required to complete the remaining work in time?
e_en: Let total work be 3 As we know, ⇒ [M₁ × D₁]/W₁ = [M₂ × D₂]/W₂ ⇒ [105 × 25]/1 = [M₂ × 35]/2 ⇒ M₂ = [105 × 25 × 2]/35 ⇒ M₂ = 150 Number of extra labours = 150 – 105 = 45

q_en: The price that Kamal should mark on a chair which costs him Rs. 1500 to gain 15% after allowing a discount of 25% (in Rs.) is:
e_en: Given: Cost price of the chair = Rs. 1500 Gain = 15% Discount = 25% Formula used: M.P = {C.P × (100 + markup%)}/100% S.P = {M.P × (100 - discount%)}/100% Discount% = {(M.P - S.P)/M.P} × 100% Profit% = {(S.P - C.P)/C.P} × 100% Where M.P = Marked price, S.P = Selling price, C.P = Cost price Calculation: Cost price = Rs. 1500 Gain = 15% ⇒ Profit = 0.15 × 1500 = 225 Selling price = Cost price + Profit ⇒ Selling price = 1500 + 225 = Rs.

q_en: In an office, there are 216 tables and 264 chairs. If 1/6 of the tables and 1/4 of the chairs are broken then how many people can work in the office if each person requires one table and one chair?
e_en: Number of fresh table = 216 × 5/6 = 180 Number of fresh chair = 264 × 3/4 = 198 If each person requires one table and one chair then number of required persons = 180

q_en: What is the least number of square tiles required to pave the floor of a room 15 m 17 cm long and 9 m 2 cm broad?
e_en: Diagram As we know, ⇒ 1 m = 100 cm ⇒ 15 m 17 cm = 1517 cm ⇒ 9 m 2 cm = 902 cm HCF of 1517 and 902 is 41 Side of square tiles is 41 Area of room = 1517 × 902 Area of tiles = 41 × 41 Number of required tiles = (1517 × 902)/(41 × 41) = 814

q_en: A and B together can complete some work in 36 days, B and C together can complete the same work in 60 days, A and C together can complete the same work in 45 days. In how many days B alone can complete the same work?
e_en: Diagram Total work = 180 Efficiency of A + B + C = (5 + 3 + 4)/2 = 6 Efficiency of B = 6 – 4 = 2 B alone can complete the whole work in = 180/2 = 90 days

q_en: A sold his pen at a profit of Rs. 13. He calculated the profit percentage on selling price and found it to be 20%. The cost price (in Rs) of the pen is:
e_en: Given: Profit = Rs. 13 Profit percent on SP = 20% Formula used: Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100 Profit % on SP = (Profit/SP) × 100 CP = SP – Profit CP is Cost Price and SP is Selling Price Calculation: Profit % on SP = (Profit/SP) × 100 20 = (13/SP) × 100 ⇒ SP = 65 CP = SP – Profit = 65 – 13 = 52 ∴ Cost price of pen is Rs. 52 Let SP of the pen be 5 unit Profit on the pen = 5 × 1/5 = 1 unit CP of the pen = 4 unit ⇒ 1 unit = Rs. 13 ⇒ 4 unit = 13 × 4 = Rs.

q_en: A sum of Rs. 50,000 is lent partly at 4% and remaining at 5% per annum. If the yearly simple interest on the average is 4.6% the two parts are:
e_en: Using allegation method 5% 4% 4.6% 0.6 : 0.4 Ratio of sum given by 5% lent to that of 4% = 0.6 : 0.4 = 3 : 2 ⇒ 3 + 2 = 5 unit ⇒ 5 unit = 50,000 ⇒ 1 unit = 10,000 ⇒ 3 unit = 10,000 × 3 = 30,000 ⇒ 2 unit = 10,000 × 2 = 20,000 ∴ Two parts are 30,000 and 20,000.

q_en: Each wheel of a bus is making 7 revolutions per second. If the diameter of a wheel is 56 cm, then the speed of the bus (in cm/sec) would be:
e_en: Radius of the wheel r = 56/2 = 28 cm Circumference of the wheel = 2πr = 2 × 22/7 × 28 = 176 cm Distance covered by the wheel in 1 revolution = 176 Distance covered by wheel in 7 revolutions = 176 × 7 = 1232 cm Speed of bus = 1232 cm/sec

If three numbers are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5 and the twice of their sum is 200. The square of the largest of three numbers is:
e_en: Given: Ratio of three numbers is 2 : 3 : 5 Twice of their sum is 200 Calculation: ⇒ 2 + 3 + 5 = 10 unit According to the question, ⇒ 10 unit = 200/2 ⇒ 1 unit = 10 ⇒ 5 unit = 50 The square of the largest of three numbers is 2500.

q_en: Out of four numbers, the average of the first three is 16 and that of the last three is 15. If the last number is 21 then the first number is:
e_en: Concept: Average = Sum of observation / Number of observations

q_en: Two trains each having length of 160 meters moving in the opposite direction crossed each other in 9 seconds. If one train crossed a 200-meter-long platform in 18 seconds, then the ratio of their speeds is:
e_en: Length of each train is 160 m Let speed of first and second train be x m/sec and y m/sec respectively. As we know, Speed = Distance/time ⇒ x = (160 + 200)/18 ⇒ x = 360/18 ⇒ x = 20 m/sec ⇒ (x + y) = (160 + 160)/9 ⇒ 9 (20 + y) = 320 ⇒ 180 + 9y = 320 ⇒ 9y = 320 – 180 ⇒ y = 140/9 m/sec Speed ratio of x : y = 20 : 140/9 = 9 : 7

q_en: What is the ratio of the total export of tea in 2012, 2014 and 2015 to the total export of coffee in 2013 and 2014?
e_en: Total export of tea in 2012, 2014 and 2015 = 400 + 500 + 420 = 1320 Total export of coffee in 2013 and 2014 = 470 + 630 = 1100 ∴ Required ratio = 1320 : 1100 = 6 : 5

q_en: The total export of coffee is approximately what percent more than the total export of tea during the give years?
e_en: Total export of coffee during the years = 450 + 470 + 630 + 500 + 600 = 2650 Total export of tea during the years = 400 + 350 + 500 + 420 + 480 = 2150 Required percentage = [(2650 – 2150)/2150] × 100 ≈ 23%

q_en: The number of years, in each of which the export of coffee is more than 20% as compared to the export of tea in that year is:
e_en: In 2013, export of tea = 350 and export of coffee = 470 Export of coffee is more than that of tea by = (470 – 350/350) × 100 = 34.28% In 2014, export of tea = 500 and export of coffee = 630 Export of coffee is more than that of tea by = (630 – 500)/500 × 100 = 26% In 2016, export of tea = 480 and export of coffee = 600 Export of coffee is more than that of tea by = (600 – 480)/480 × 100 = 25% So, there are 3 years.

q_en: A sum of Rs 5200 is divided amongst A, B, C, and D such that the ratio of shares of A and B is 2 : 3, that of B and C is 4 : 5 and that of C and D is 1 : 2. What is the difference between the shares of B and D?
e_en: Given: The total sum of money = Rs. 5200 The ratio of the share of A and B = 2 ∶ 3 The ratio of the share of B and C = 4 ∶ 5 The ratio of the share of C and D = 1 ∶ 2 Calculations: Simplifying the ratios to get the same unit by cross multiplication Ratio of A and B = (2 ∶ 3) × 4 ⇒ 8 ∶ 12 Ratio of B and C = (4 ∶ 5) × 3 ⇒ 12 ∶ 15 Ratio of C and D = (1 ∶ 2) × 15 ⇒ 15 ∶ 30 Ratio of A, B, C and D = 8 ∶ 12 ∶ 15 ∶ 30 Total sum = 8x + 12x + 15x + 30x ⇒ 65x = 5200 ⇒ x = 80 Difference…

q_en: A person travels a certain distance at a speed of 18 km/h and returns to the starting point at 12 km/h. If he takes 2 hours 55 minutes for the whole journey, the distance one way is:
e_en: ⇒ 2 hr + 55 min = 2 + 55/60 = 2 + 11/12 = 35/12 Let total distance be x km, then According to the question ⇒ x/18 + x/12 = 35/12 ⇒ (2x + 3x)/36 = 35/12 ⇒ 5x/36 = 35/12 ⇒ x = 35/12 × 36/5 ⇒ x = 21 km Short Trick : Required distance = [(12 × 18)/(12 + 18)] × 35/12 = 21 km

q_en: In an examination, the average score of students in a class who passed is 69 and that of who failed is 61. If the average score of all the students, who appeared in examination is 66, then the percentage of students who passed is:
e_en: Using allegation method 69 61 66 5 : 3 Ratio of students who passed to fail = 5 : 3 Let passed students = 5, Failed students = 3 Hence, total students = 8 Percentage of passed students = (5/8) × 100 = 62.5%

q_en: In a 60 litre solution of acid and water, the ratio of acid and water is 3 : 7. How much (in litre) acid is to be mixed in the solution so that the ratio of acid and water in the ration of acid and water in the resulting solution is 1 : 2?
e_en: Total solution = 60 Quantity of acid = 60 × 3/10 = 18 Quantity of water = 60 – 18 = 42 Let quantity of acid added be x litres. According to the question ⇒ (18 + x)/42 = 1/2 ⇒ 36 + 2x = 42 ⇒ 2x = 42 – 36 ⇒ x = 6/2 ⇒ x = 3 litres

q_en: The average of 20 numbers is 80. The average of the first 10 numbers is 76.5 and next 7 numbers is 82. The 18th number is 3 more than the 19th number but 3 less than the 20th number. What is the average of 18th and 19th numbers?
e_en: Sum of 20 numbers = 20 × 80 = 1600 Sum of first 10 numbers = 10 × 76.5 = 765 Sum of next 7 numbers = 7 × 82 = 574 Sum of 18th, 19th and 20th = 1600 – 765 – 574 = 261 Let 18th number be x ⇒ 19th number = x – 3 ⇒ 20th number = x + 3 ⇒ x + x – 3 + x + 3 = 261 ⇒ 3x = 261 ⇒ x = 87 Average of 18th and 19th number = (87 + 84)/2 = 85.5

q_en: In 729 litres solution of acid and water, the ratio of acid and water is 7 : 2. How many litres of water must be added to it to get the solution in which the ratio of acid and water is 5 : 3?
e_en: Quantity of acid in the solution = 729 × 7/9 = 567 litres Quantity of water in the solution = 729 - 567 = 162 litres Let quantity of added water be x, then ⇒ 567/(162 + x) = 5/3 ⇒ 3 × 567 = 5 × 162 + 5x ⇒ 1701 = 810 + 5x ⇒ 5x = 1701 - 810 ⇒ x = 178.2 ∴ The quantity of added water is 178.2 litres.

q_en: The ratio of the number of boys and girls in a class is 2 : 3 and the average score in mathematics of all the students in the class is 54. The average score of boys is 50% more than the average score of girls. What is the average score of girls?
e_en: Let average score of girls be 2x Average score of boys = 2x × 3/2 = 3x Ratio of boys and girls = 2 : 3 Let number of boys be = 2 and number of girls = 3 According to the question ⇒ 2 × 3x + 3 × 2x = 54 × 5 ⇒ 6x + 6x = 270 ⇒ 12x = 270 ⇒ x = 270/12 Average score of girls = 2 × 270/12 = 45

q_en: A boat goes a distance of 3 km upstream and 4 1/2 km downstream in 45 minutes, while it goes 3.6 km upstream and 2.4 km downstream in 39 minutes. The speed (in km/h) of the boat when going downstream is:
e_en: Let speed of boat and stream be x km/hr and y km/hr, Upstream speed = (x - y) km/hr Downstream speed = (x + y) km/hr According to the question ⇒ 3/(x - y) + 4.5/(x + y) = 45/60 --- (1) ⇒ 3.6/(x - y) + 2.4/(x + y) = 39/60 --- (2) After multiply by 1.2 in equation (1) subtract equation (2) from equation (1) ⇒ 3/(x + y) = 1/4 ⇒ x + y = 12 km/hr ∴ Downstream speed is 12 km/hr.

q_en: A can do a piece of work in 30 days. He completed 40% of the work and then left. B completed the remaining work in 21 days. Working together, A and B will complete 65% of the same work in:

q_en: A, B and C can do a work in 12, 15 and 20 days respectively. In how many days, working together they can complete the same work?

e_en: Given: Divisor: remainder = 3 : 2 ----- (i) Divisor: quotient = 7 : 12 ----- (ii) Multiply equation (i) by 7 and equation (ii) by 3 ⇒ Divisor : remainder : quotient = 21 : 14 : 36 Divident = divisor × quotient + remainder ⇒ 21 × 36 + 14 = 770 According to question ⇒ 770/9 = 85 + 5/9 ∴ Remainder in this case = 5

q_en: If, a : b = 2 : 3, then (3a + 4b)/(4a + 5b) is equal to:
e_en: Given: A : b = 2 : 3 Calculation: Putting the value of a and b 2 and 3 respectively in the equation, we get ⇒ {3 × 2 + 4 × 3}/{4 × 2 + 5 × 3} ⇒ {18}/{23} ⇒ 18 : 23

q_en: Ramesh is thrice as old as Suresh. Two years hence, Ramesh will be twice as old as Suresh. Ramesh’s present age (in years) is:
e_en: Given: Ramesh is thrice as old as Suresh After two years Ramesh will be twice of Suresh Calculation: Let the present age of Ramesh be 3x and of Suresh be x According to question: ⇒ (3x + 2)/(x + 2) = 2 / 1 ⇒ 3x + 2 = 2x + 4 ⇒ x = 2 ∴ Ramesh’s age = 3 × 2 = 6 years

q_en: A man bought 15 articles at ₹ 70 each, 13 at ₹ 60 each and 12 at ₹ 65 each. The average price per article (in ₹) is:
e_en: Given: 15 article bought at Rs. 70 each 13 article bought at Rs. 60 each 12 article bought at Rs. 65 each Formula used: Average = total sum/total number Calculation: Cost of 15 articles = 15 × 70 = Rs. 1050 Cost of 13 articles = 13 × 60 = Rs. 780 Cost of 12 articles = 12 × 65 = Rs. 780 Total of all the articles = 1050 + 780 + 780 = Rs. 2610 Total number of articles = 15 + 13 + 12 = 40 ∴ Required average = 2610/40 = 65.25

q_en: A and B can complete a work in 20 days and 30 days respectively. A works full time but B works half time. In how many days the entire work is to be completed?
e_en: Given: A can complete the work in 20 days B can complete the work in 30 days Calculation: LCM of 20 and 30 = 60 Let the total work be 60 units Efficiency of A = 60/20 = 3 units/day Efficiency of B = 60/30 = 2 units/day But according to question A work full day and B works for half day. ∴ Efficiency of A = 3 And, efficiency of B = 1 So, now the new efficiency of A and B when they worked together = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day ∴ Work will complete in = 60 / 4 = 15 days

q_en: A solid brass sphere of radius 15 cm is drawn into a wire of diameter 6 mm. The length (in cm) of the wire is:
e_en: Given: Radius of sphere = 15 cm Diameter of wire = 6mm Concept used: Volume of sphere is 4/3 × π × r³ Volume of cylinder is π × r² × l Calculation: Radius = Diameter/2 = 6/2 = 3 mm = 0.3 cm Volume of sphere = Volume of wire (cylinder) ⇒ 4/3 × π × 15³ = π × 0.3² × l ⇒ l = 50000 cm

q_en: In how many years, an amount becomes three times of itself, if simple interest is calculated at a rate of 10% per annum?
e_en: Given: Principal becomes 3 times of itself Rate% = 10% Formula used: Simple interest = (principal × time × rate)/100 Calculation: Let the principal be x According to question Simple interest = Amount – principal ∴ Simple interest = 3x – x = 2x Now, 2x = (x × 10 × time)/100 ⇒ Time = 20 years

q_en: The average temperature of first three days of the week is 23° C; the average temperature of next three days is 24° C and the average temperature of whole week is 23.5° C. The temperature on the last day of the week is:
e_en: Given: Average temperature of first three days = 23°C Average temperature of next three days = 24°C Calculation: Total temperature of 1st 6 days of week = 23 × 3 + 24 × 3 = 141 Total temperature of week = 7 × 23.5 = 164.5 ∴ Temperature of last day = 164.5 – 141 = 23.5

q_en: A box contains 780 bananas out of which 130 bananas are rotten and rest are of good quality. The percentage (correct to two decimal places) of good quality of bananas is:
e_en: Given: Box contains 780 bananas Rotten bananas = 130 Calculation: Good quality bananas = 780 – 130 = 650 ∴ Percentage of good quality bananas = (650/780) × 100 = 83.33%

q_en: A man buys a single article at ₹ 16. If he were to buy a dozen articles, he would have to pay a total amount of ₹ 160. What would be the approximate percent discount (correct to nearest integer) he would get on buying a dozen articles?
e_en: Given: A single article can be bought at Rs. 16 If a dozen article he bought he have to give Rs. 160 Calculation: According to question Cost of one article = Rs. 16 Cost of 12 articles = 16 × 12 = Rs. 192 But he gave Rs. 160 Hence, discount = 192 – 160 = 32 ∴ Discount percentage = [(32/192)] × 100 = 16.66% ≈ 17%

q_en: A train 180 m long moving at the speed of 20 m/sec passes across a boy who is moving at a speed of 10 m/sec in the direction of the train. The time (in s) taken by the train to overtake the boy is:
e_en: Given: Length of train = 180 m Speed of train = 20 m/sec Speed of boy = 10 m/sec Calculation: When train and boy moves in the same direction, then relative speed = 20 – 10 = 10 m/sec We know, distance = speed × time ⇒ 180 = 10 × time ∴ Time = 18 sec

q_en: If Shivan walks at the rate of 19 km/h. How much time (in minutes) will he take to cover 665 m?
e_en: Given: Shivam walking speed = 19 km/hr Speed in m/sec = 19 × (5/18) = 95/18 m/sec Calculation: We know, distance = speed × time ⇒ 665 = (95/18) × time ⇒ Time = (665 × 18)/95 = 126 sec Or, Time = 126/60 = 2(1)/({10)} min

q_en: The cost price of a camera is 90% of its selling price. The profit percentage is:

q_en: What is the present value of the amount of Rs 14739 payable in the 3 years at the rate of 6.25% compound annual interest?
e_en: Given: Final amount = Rs.14739 Rate of interest = 6.25% Time = 3 years Formula used: Amount = Principal [1 + (R/100)]Time Solution: Let principal be P so, P [1 + (6.25/100)]³ = Rs.14739 ⇒ P [106.25/100]³ = Rs.14739 ⇒ P × (17/16)³ = Rs.14739 ⇒ P = Rs.(3 × 16³) ⇒ P = Rs.12288 ∴ The present value is Rs.12288

q_en: Suppose x is the largest 4-digit number, divided by 7, 8 and 11 leaving 4, 5 and 8 remainder respectively. When x is divided by (7 + 8 + 11), the remainder will be:
e_en: Given: A 4-digit number x when divided by 7, 8, and 11 leaves the remainder of 4, 5, and 8 respectively Solution: L.C.M of 7, 8, and 11 = 616 Largest 4-digit number = 9999 and 9999 = 616 × 16 + 143 and 616 × 16 = 9856 Now, difference between (7 – 4) = (8 – 5) = (11 – 8) = 3 so, Reducing 3 from 9856 = 9853 Now, when 9853 is divided by 26, then 9853 = 26 × 378 + 25 So, The remainder will be 25

q_en: The marked price of an article was 42% more than its cost price. If there is a profit of 20.7% on selling the item, then the percentage of discount given on the marked price of the article is:
e_en: Given: The marked price of an article was 42% more than its cost price Profit % = 20.7 % Concept: Discount is always done on Marked price Formula used: Discount % = [(M.P - S.P)/M.P] × 100 Calculation: Let Cost Price, C.P be 100 ⇒ M.P = 42 % More than C.P ⇒ 100 + (42/100) × 100 = 142 Profit % = 20.7 % ⇒ S.P = 100 + (20.7/100) × 100 = 120.7 ∴ Discount = M.P - S.P = 142 - 120.7 = 21.3 Discount % = (21.3/142) × 100 = 15%

e_en: Given: Sonu sold the bike at 13.5% loss If S.P would have been Rs.8900 more, gain % = 31% Final S.P = Rs.20,740 Concept used: Gain % = (Gain/C.P) × 100 Solution: Let C.P of bike be 100x So, S.P = 100x × (100 – 13.5)/100 = 86.5x And if, S.P would have been Rs.8900 more, Gain% = 31% So, New S.P = 100x × (100 + 31)/100 = 131x Now, New S.P – S.P = Rs.8900 ⇒ 131x – 86.5x = 8900 ⇒ 44.5x = Rs.8900 ⇒ 100x = Rs.(8900/44.5x) × 100x ⇒ Rs.20,000 So, C.P = Rs.20,000 Final S.P = Rs.20,740…

q_en: A cylindrical bucket, with a height of 27 cm and a base radius of 48 cm, is filled with sand. When the bucket is emptied to the ground and a conical pile of radius 54 cm is formed. What is the height (in cm) of the pile?

q_en: If 4 men can reap a field in 5 days working 9 hours a day, in how many hours can 10 men reap the same field working 3 days?
e_en: Given: Time taken by 4 men working 9 hours a day = 5 days Formula used: (M1 × D1 × H1)/W1 = (M2 × D2 × H2)/W2 Calculation: (4 × 5 × 9)/1 = (10 × 3 × H2)/1 ⇒ H2 = (4 × 5 × 9)/(10 × 3) ⇒ H2 = 6 ∴ The required number of hours is 6.

q_en: A train takes 1 hour 30 minutes to travel between two stations P and Q. If it travels at 5/6 of its usual speed, how long will it take to travel between P and Q?
e_en: Given: Time taken by the train to travel from P and Q = 1 hour 30 minutes Formula used: Distance/Speed = Time When the distance is constant, Time = 1/speed Calculation: Let the usual speed be = 6 units ⇒ Reduced speed = 6 × 5/6 = 5 units Time taken by the train with usual speed = 1 hour 30 minutes So, 5 = 3/2 hours ⇒ 6 = 3/2 × 6/5 ⇒ 6 = 1 hour 48 minutes ∴ Time taken to travel from P to Q with reduced speed is 1 hour 48 minutes.

q_en: In an election, the votes cast for two candidates were in the ratio 4 ∶ 9. If the successful candidate received 984321 votes, then the total votes received by the unsuccessful candidate is:
e_en: Given: Ratio of votes cast for two candidates = 4 : 9 Votes received by successful candidate = 984321 Calculation: The candidate who gets maximum votes will become successful. ⇒ 9 = 984321 ⇒ 1 = 109369 ⇒ 4 = 4 × 109369 = 437476 ∴ The votes received by unsuccessful candidate is 437476.

q_en: What is the sum of the numbers between 300 and 400 such that when they are divided by 6, 12 and 16, it leaves no remainder?
e_en: Given: Numbers between 300 and 400. Formula used: HCF: Product of the smallest power of each common prime factor in the numbers. LCM: Product of the greatest power of each prime factor, involved in the numbers. Calculation: By Prime Factorization: 6 = 2 × 3 12 = 2² × 3 16 = 2⁴ LCM of 6, 12 and 16 = 24 × 3 = 48 Multiples of 48 between 300 and 400 which are: 336, 384 ∴ The required sum = 336 + 384 ⇒ 720

q_en: A certain sum amounts to Rs. 29,282 in 4 years at 10% p.a. when the interest is compounded yearly. What is the simple interest (in Rs.) on double of the sum for five years’ time at the same rate?
e_en: Given: Amount in 4 years at 10% per annum = Rs.29282 Formulas used: Amount on compound interest (compounded yearly) P × (1 + r/100)ⁿ Simple Interest = P × Rate/100 × Time Calculation: Rs.29282 = P × (1 + 10/100)⁴ ⇒ 29282 = P × 14641/10000 ⇒ P = 29282 × 10000/14641 ⇒ P = 20000 Simple interest at double the sum for 5 years at 10% p.a: ⇒ 2 × 20000 × 5 × 10/100 ⇒ 20000 ∴ The required simple interest is Rs.20000.

q_en: A person borrows Rs. 75,000 for 3 years at 7% simple interest. He lends it to B at 5% for 3 years. What is his loss (in Rs.)?
e_en: Given: Principal borrowed for 3 years at 7% simple interest = Rs.75000 Lending rate of the same principal for 3 years = 5% Formula used: Simple Interest = Principal × Rate/100 × Time Calculation: Simple interest payable = 75000 × 7/100 × 3 ⇒ Rs.15750 Simple interest Receivable = 75000 × 5/100 × 3 ⇒ Rs.11250 ∴ Loss incurred by the person = Interest payable - Interest receivable ⇒ Rs.15750 - 11250 = Rs.4500

q_en: The selling price of an article is Rs. 2,300 and profit percentage is 25%. If the article is sold again for Rs.1,656, then what is the loss/gain percentage?
e_en: Given: Selling Price 1 = Rs.2300 Profit percentage = 25% Selling Price 2 = Rs.1656 Formulas used: Selling Price = Cost Price × (100 + Profit)% Loss = Cost Price - Selling Price Loss Percentage = Loss/Cost Price × 100 Calculation: Cost Price = 2300 × 100%/(100 + 25)% ⇒ Rs.1840 Loss = Rs.1840 - Rs.1656 = Rs.184 ∴ Loss percentage = 184/1840 × 100 ⇒ 10%

q_en: Due to 20% reduction in the price of wheat per kg, Ram is able to buy 5 kg more for Rs.800. What is the original quantity (in kg) of wheat?

q_en: The average of the 2-digit numbers 37, 45, 6x and x6 is 48. What is the average of (4x + 3) and (x + 7)?
e_en: Given: Average of numbers 37, 45, 6x and x6 = 48 Formula used: Average of observations = Sum of observations/Number of observations Calculation: The numbers 6x and x6 can be written as 60 + x and 10x + 6 in terms of the sum of unit digit and ten's digit. Now, (37 + 45 + 60 + x + 10x + 6)/4 = 48 ⇒ 148 + 11x = 48 × 4 ⇒ 148 + 11x = 192 ⇒ 11x = 192 - 148 ⇒ x = 44/11 ⇒ x = 4 Average of (4x + 3) and (x + 7) = (4 × 4 + 3 + 4 + 7)/2 ⇒ 30/2 ⇒ 15 ∴ The required result is 15.

(100 × 82.5) ⇒ Rs. 8,250 ∴ The Cost price of an article is Rs. 8,250

q_en: A, B and C are three boxes containing marbles in the ratio 3 : 5 : 7, and the total number of marbles is 75. If 3 marbles are transferred from B to A, and 5 marbles are transferred from C to B, then the new ratio of the marbles is:

q_en: The average of seven consecutive odd numbers is 27. If the last number is removed from the list, then the average of the remaining numbers is:
e_en: Given: The average of seven consecutive odd numbers = 27 Formula used: Average = sum of observations/Number of observations Calculation: Let the 7 numbers are (x - 6), (x - 4), (x - 2), x, (x + 2), (x + 4), (x + 6) Now, the sum = 7x 27 = 7x/7 x = 27 The last number is removed from the list, that means (x + 6) is removed New sum = (x - 6) + (x - 4)+(x - 2)+ x +(x + 2) + (x + 4) Average = (6x - 6)/6 = (162 - 6)/6 = 26

q_en: The numbers 25, 34, 46, 48, 2x+1, 4x+3, 105, 110, 114, 122 are written in ascending order and their median is 77. The value of x is:

q_en: If the difference between the selling prices of an article when sold at 18% discount and at 10.5% discount is Rs. 192, then the marked price of the article is:
e_en: Given: Discount percentages are 18% and 10.5% Concept used: SP = MP - MP × Discount% Calculation: Let marked price be 100x So, SP = 100x - 18x = 82x [When Discount = 18%] SP = 100x - 10.5x = 89.5x [When Discount = 10.5%] According to the question, 89.5x - 82x = 192 ⇒ 7.5x = 192 ⇒ 100x = 2560 ∴ The marked price of the article is Rs.2560

q_en: The average of 40% of a number and 33% of the same number is 73. The average of 1/5th and 1/4th of that number is:

q_en: A man takes a loan of Rs. 6,000 from his friend on 1st January 2019 with the condition that he will repay with accrued simple interest at the rate 6.25% per annum, as and when the interest touches Rs. 75. On which date does the loan period expire?

q_en: When a reactangle is divided into three equal parts, each of them turns out to be a square of area 16 cm². What is the perimeter (in cm) of the rectangle?

q_en: Two circles of radii 10 cm and 12 cm intersect each other and the length of their common chord is 16 cm. What is the distance (in cm) between their centres?
e_en: Given: PA = 10 cm QA = 12 cm AB = 16 cm Concept used: Pythagoras Theorem Distance between two centres divides the common chord in halves and is perpendicular to the common chord as well. Calculation: AR = RB = 16 ÷ 2 = 8 cm AB is perpendicular to PQ. Hence, PQ divides AB in halves. Now, PR = sqrt {10² - 8²} = 6 cm QR = sqrt {12² - 8² } = 4√5 cm Thus, PQ = (6 + 4√5) cm ∴ The distance between their centres is (6 + 4√5) cm.

q_en: The marked price of an article is ₹400. After allowing a discount of 20% on the marked price, a shopkeeper makes a profit of ₹48. His gain percentage is:
e_en: Given: M.P = Rs. 400 and discount = 20% Concept used: Gain% = [(S.P. – C.P)/C.P] ×100 S.P = [(100 - D%)/M.P] × 100 Profit = S.P - C.P Where C.P = Cost Price, S.P = Selling Price, M.P = Marked Price, D% = Discount % Calculation: According to the question, S.P = [(100 - D%)/M.P] × 100 S.P = M.P. × 80/100 ⇒ 400 × 80/100 ⇒ Rs. 320 C.P. = S.P. – Profit ⇒ 320 - 48 ⇒ Rs. 272 Gain percentage = (48/272) × 100 = 17 11/17% ∴ Required gain percentage is 17 11/17%

e_en: ​Given: 4 men can reap a field in 5 days working 9 hours a day Formula used: (M₁ × D₁ × H₁)/W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂)/W₂ Calculation: (4 × 5 × 9)/1 = (10 × D₂ × 6)/1 ⇒ D2 = (4 × 5 × 9)/(10 × 6) ⇒ D2 = 3 ∴ The required number of days are 3.

e_en: Given: Distance between place A and B = 90 km Speed of Sita = Speed of Geeta - 3 km/h Formula used: Ratio of distance = Ratio of speed (When the time is equal) Calculation: Distance travelled by Sita = 75 km Distance travelled by Geeta = 90 + 15 = 105 km Ratio of Distance in a certain time travelled by Sita and Geeta is equal to the ratio of the speed = 75 : 105 ⇒ 5 : 7 ⇒ 7 - 5 = 2 units = 3 km/h ⇒ 1 unit = 1.5 km/h ⇒ 5 = 5 × 1.5 = 7.5 km/h ∴ The speed of Sita is 7.5 km/h.

q_en: If the ratio of an external angle and an internal angle of a regular polygon is 1 : 5, then what is the number of sides in the polygon?
e_en: Given: external angle : internal angle = 1 : 5 Formula used for regular Polygon: External angle = 360/n Internal angle ={(n - 2)/n}180 Where n is the number of sides in a polygon. Calculation: According to the question, 360/n : {(n - 2)/n}180 = 1 : 5 ⇒ 2/(n - 2) = 1 : 5 ⇒ (n - 2) = 10 ⇒ n = 12 ∴ The number of sides in the polygon is 12.

q_en: The selling price of an item is 20% less than its marked price. The marked price of the item is 30% more than the cost price. What is the profit percentage?
e_en: Formula used: Gain% = (Gain/CP) × 100 Calculation: Let cost price of the items is 100 Rs According to the question, Marked price = 100 + 30% ×100 MP = 100 + 30 = 130 Rs A selling price 20% less than the marked price means 80% of the marked price is the selling price SP = 80% × 130 SP = 104 Rs Gain = Selling price - Cost price Gain = 104 - 100 = 4 Gain% = (4/100) × 100 Gain% = 4% ∴ Profit Percentage is 4%.

q_en: If 45% of (x - y) = 30% of (x + y), then what percent of x is y?
e_en: Given: 45% of (x - y) = 30% of (x + y) Calculation: 45% of (x - y) = 30% of (x + y) ⇒(45/100) × (x - y) = (30/100) × (x + y) Divide the above equation by 15 and 100 will be cut from both sides, 3(x - y) = 2(x + y) ⇒3x - 3y = 2x + 2y ⇒3x - 2x = 2y + 3y ⇒ x = 5y ⇒ x/y = 5/1 ⇒Percentage of x is y = (1/5) × 100 ⇒ 20% ∴ The percentage of x is y is 20%.

q_en: A girl goes from M to N at a speed of 25 km/h and returns to M at a speed of 37.5 km/h, via the same route. What is the girl’s average speed (in km/h)?

q_en: Find the smallest natural number ‘x’ that must be subtracted from 1800 so that (1800 - x), when divided by 7, 11 and 23, will leave 5 as the remainder in each case.

e_en: Given: The diagonals of a rhombus are 16 cm The side of the rhombus is 10 cm Calculation: Since, we know that d12 + d22 = 4a2, where d1 and d2 are the diagonals of rhombus and a is the side ⇒ 162 + d22 = 4 × 102 ⇒ d22 = 400 – 256 ⇒ d2 = 12 Now, the area of rhombus = ½ × d1 × d2 The area of rhombus = ½ × 16 × 12 ∴ The area of rhombus is 96 cm2

q_en: The mean temperature from Monday to Thursday is 39.25°C. The mean temperature from Thursday to Sunday is 40.25°C. If the sum of the daily temperatures of all the days during the week, from Monday to Sunday, is 277.5°C, then what is the temperature for Thursday?

e_en: Given: Total runs scored = 120 Number of fours = 6 Number of sixes = 4 Calculation: Runs scored by fours = 6 × 4 = 24 Runs scored by sixes = 4 × 6 = 24 Total runs scored by boundaries and sixes = 24 + 24 = 48 Runs scored by running between the wickets = 120 – 48 = 72 Required percentage = (72/120) × 100% = 60% ∴ Batsman scored 60% runs by running between the wickets.

q_en: Find the smallest number which when divided by 19 and 23 gives remainders of 13 and 17, respectively.

q_en: A solid copper sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and redrawn into a wire, whose radius of cross-section is 8 cm. Find the length of the wire.

Concept used: Volume of sphere = (4/3) × πR3 Volume of cylinder = πr2h Calculation: As we know, Volume of sphere = (4/3) × πR³ Volume of cylinder = πr²h ⇒ R = 6 and, r = 8 According to the question, ⇒ πr²h = (4/3) πR³ ⇒ 8 × 8 × h = (4/3) × 6 × 6 × 6 ⇒ h = (4 × 2 × 6 × 6)/(8 × 8) ⇒ h = 4.5 cm ∴ The length of the wire is 4.5 cm.

q_en: The diameter of a circle is 112 cm. What is the circumference of this circle? [Use π = 22/7]
e_en: Given: The diameter of a circle is 112 cm. Concept used: Circumference of a circle = 2πr Here, R = radius Calculation: Radius of the circle = 112/2 ⇒ 56 Circumference = 2 × 22/7 × 56 ⇒ 2 × 22 × 8 ⇒ 352 ∴ The circumference of the circle is 352 cm.

q_en: If the selling price of a shirt is reduced from Rs. 440 to Rs. 410, the loss increases by 4%. What is the cost price of the shirt?
e_en: Given: If the selling price of a shirt is reduced from Rs. 440 to Rs. 410, the loss increases by 4%. Calculation: Let the cost price be 100% According to the question, At loss of 4% ⇒ 4% = 440 – 410 ⇒ 4% = 30 ⇒ 1% = 7.5 ⇒ 100% = 7.5 × 100 ⇒ Rs. 750 ∴ The cost price of the shirt is Rs. 750.

q_en: The marked price of a table is 130% of its cost price. A discount of 20% is given on the sale of the table. What will be the profit percentage?
e_en: Given: The marked price of a table is 130% of its cost price. A discount of 20% is given on the sale of the table. Calculation: Let the cost price be 100a So, marked price = 100a × 130% ⇒ 130a Selling price = 130a × 80% ⇒ 104a Profit = 104a - 100a ⇒ 4a Profit % = (4a/100a) × 100 ⇒ 4% ∴ The profit percentage is 4%.

q_en: A fan is sold for Rs. 1,560 at a profit of 30%. If its selling price is Rs. 960, then what will be the loss percentage?

Therefore, Sonu can do (120/15) = 8 units of work in a day. Monu can do (120/10) = 12 units of work in a day. Tipu can do (120/12) = 10 units of work in a day. Hence, together, Sonu, Monu and Tipu can do (8+12+10) = 30 units of work in a day.

Concept used: Total = Average × Number of entities Calculation: Sum of 11 observations = 11 × 10 = 110 Sum of the first 6 observations = 6 × 9 = 54 Sum of the last 6 observations = 6 × 11 = 66 Now, the 6th observation = (54 + 66 - 110) = 10 ∴ The 6th observation is 10.

q_en: How much amount can a person get on a sum of Rs. 6,600, if it is invested at 6.2% per annum for a period of 2 years 6 months on simple interest?

e_en: Given data: Sajid drives for 6 hours at 60 km/hr Sajid drives for 4 hours at 50 km/hr Concept: Average speed = Total distance / Total time Solution: ⇒ Total distance covered = (6 hours × 60 km/hr) + (4 hours × 50 km/hr) = 360 km + 200 km = 560 km ⇒ Total time = 6 hours + 4 hours = 10 hours ⇒ Average speed = 560 km / 10 hours = 56 km/hr Therefore, Sajid's average speed for the whole journey is 56 km/hr.

q_en: The average of 24 numbers is 43. If we subtract a number 'M' from each number, then the average becomes 38. What was the value of M?
e_en: Given: Average of 24 numbers = 43 New average when 'M' is subtracted from each number = 38 Concept used: Properties of averages Solution: ⇒ When a constant is subtracted from each number in a set, the average of the set decreases by that constant ⇒ Therefore, the value of M = 43 - 38 = 5 Therefore, the value of M is 5

q_en: X and Y together can do a piece of work in 30 days. Z alone can do it in 60 days. If they worked together, then in how many days they can finish the work?
e_en: Given: X and Y can do a work in 30 days, Z can do it alone in 60 days. Formula: (1/(X+Y)) + (1/Z) = 1/Total Calculation: ⇒ (1/30) + (1/60) = 1/Total ⇒ Total = 20 days. Hence, they can finish the work in 20 days.

q_en: Anil alone takes 2 hrs 40 min to complete a work and sumit alone can complete the same work in half time of Anil How much time will be taken by sumit to complete the work?
e_en: Given: Anil takes 2 hrs 40 min to complete a work Sumit completes the work in half the time taken by Anil Concept: Basic time conversion and division Solution: ⇒ Time taken by Anil = 2 hrs 40 min = 160 min ⇒ Time taken by Sumit = Half of time taken by Anil = 160/2 min Therefore, Sumit will take 80 minutes to complete the work

q_en: A person sold an article at a loss of 4%. Had he sold it at a gain of 1%, he would have received Rs. 42.5 more. To gain 18%, what must be his selling price?
e_en: Given: Loss of 4% = Cost Price - Selling Price, Gain of 1% = Selling Price - Cost Price Calculation: ⇒ 5% = 42.5 ⇒ Cost Price = 42.5 × (100/5) = 850 ⇒ Selling Price for 18% gain = 850 + 18% of 850 = Rs. 1003 Therefore, to gain 18%, the selling price should be Rs. 1003.

q_en: The value of [0.004 × {5 ÷ (21 - 6) × 3} + 0.8] lies between:
e_en: Given: [0.004 × {5 ÷ (21 - 6) × 3} + 0.8] Formula used: BODMAS Rule (Brackets, Orders, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction) Calculations: [0.004 × {5 ÷ 15 × 3} + 0.8] ⇒ [0.004 × {5/15 × 3} + 0.8] ⇒ [0.004 × {1/3 × 3} + 0.8] ⇒ [0.004 × 1 + 0.8] ⇒ 0.004 + 0.8 ⇒ 0.804 0.804 lies between 0.5 and 0.9 ∴ The correct answer is option (C).

q_en: What is that least number that should be added to 478 so that the number obtained becomes exactly divisible by 5, 6, and 12?
e_en: Given: The number 478 Concept used: The number should be divisible by the least common multiple (LCM) of 5, 6, and 12 solution: ⇒ LCM of 5, 6, and 12 = 60 Please note that 480 is divisible by 60. ⇒ Number to be added = 480 - 478 = 2 Therefore, 2 should be added to 478 to make it divisible by 5, 6, and 12.

e_en: Correct answer: Rs. 133.1.

q_en: If 750 is divided into two parts such that the ratio of one to the other is in the ratio 8 ∶ 7, then find the smallest number.
e_en: Given: Total number = 750, Ratio = 8 : 7 Calculation: ⇒ Smallest number = 750 × (7/15) = 350 Hence, the smallest number is 350.

q_en: A table is bought for Rs. 2450 and sold for Rs. 2940. The gain percent is:
e_en: Given: Cost price = Rs. 2450 Selling price = Rs. 2940 Formula used: Gain percent = [(Selling Price - Cost Price)/Cost Price] × 100 Solution: ⇒ Gain = Selling Price - Cost Price = Rs. 2940 - Rs. 2450 = Rs. 490 ⇒ Gain percent = (Gain/Cost Price) × 100 = (490/2450) × 100 Therefore, the gain percent is 0.2 or 20%

q_en: Successive discount of 15% and 35% is equivalent to a single discount of:
e_en: Given: Successive discounts of 15% and 35% Calculation: ⇒ Equivalent discount = 1 - (1 - 15/100) × (1 - 35/100) = 0.4475 or 44.75% Therefore, successive discounts of 15% and 35% is equivalent to a single discount of 0.4475 or 44.75%.

q_en: A sum of Rs. 11500 amounts to Rs. 12880 in 2 years at the rate of simple interest. What is the rate of interest?
e_en: Given: Principal = Rs. 11500, Amount after 2 years = Rs. 12880 Formula: Rate = 100 × (SI/PT) Calculation: ⇒ Rate = 100 × ((12880 - 11500)/(11500 × 2)) = 6% per annum Hence, the rate of interest is 6% per annum.

q_en: Two successive price decreases of 20% and 30% of an article are equivalent to a single price decrease of:
e_en: Given data: First decrease = 20% Second decrease = 30% Concept: For two successive discounts, the equivalent single discount = 1 - (1 - first decrease)(1 - second decrease) Solution: ⇒ Equivalent decrease = 1 - (1 - 0.20)(1 - 0.30) = 1 - 0.56 = 0.44 or 44% Therefore, two successive price decreases of 20% and 30% are equivalent to a single price decrease of 44%.

q_en: In a match, average runs scored by 4 batsmen is 48 . If the runs scored by three batsmen are 58,28 and 24 respectively, then how many runs did the fourth player score?
e_en: Given: Average runs of 4 batsmen = 48, Runs scored by three batsmen = 58, 28, 24 Calculation: ⇒ Runs scored by fourth player = (4 × 48) - (58 + 28 + 24) = 82 Hence, the fourth player scored 82 runs.

q_en: If A ∶ B is 7 ∶ 4 and A - B = 9, then what is the value of A + B?
e_en: Given: A ∶ B = 7 ∶ 4, A - B = 9 Calculation: ⇒ A = 9 × 7/(7 - 4) = 21 ⇒ B = 9 × 4/(7 - 4) = 12 ⇒ A + B = 21 + 12 = 33 Therefore, the value of A + B is 33.

q_en: Find the area of triangle having base 34 cm and corresponding height as 22 cm.

q_en: The average age of six brothers is 15 years. If their father is also included, the average is increased by 7 years. Find the age of the father (in years).

q_en: If interest is being compounded half yearly, then what sum will amount to Rs. 51840 in 2 years at the rate of 40 percent per annum on compound interest?
e_en: Given data: Compound amount = Rs. 51840 Time = 2 years Rate of interest = 40% per annum, compounded semiannually Concept: If interest is compounded semiannually, then A = P × (1 + R/200)⁽²T⁾ Solution: ⇒ 51840 = P × (1 + 40/200)⁽²×²⁾ ⇒ P = 51840 / (1.2)⁴ = Rs. 25000 Therefore, the sum that will amount to Rs. 51840 in 2 years at the rate of 40 percent per annum on compound interest, compounded semiannually, is Rs. 25000.

q_en: A man buys 21 mangoes for a rupee. How many mangoes had he sold for a rupee so that there is a loss of 30 percent?

q_en: A product, whose marked price is Rs. 840, is sold for Rs. 798 by a wholesale shop. What is the percentage discount given by him?
e_en: Given data: Marked price = Rs. 840 Selling price = Rs. 798 Concept: Discount percentage = (Discount / Marked price) × 100 Solution: ⇒ Discount = 840 - 798 = Rs. 42 ⇒ Discount percentage = (42 / 840) × 100 = 5% Therefore, the percentage discount given by him is 5%.

q_en: Find the value of 221 + 207 - 3 of 44 + 7 × 4

q_en: The ratio of speed of three racers is 3 ∶ 2 ∶ 4. What is the respective ratio of time taken by the three racers to cover the same distance?

q_en: HCF of 3/4, 15/16 and 18/5 is:

q_en: 30 percent of marked price is equal to 50 percent of cost price. If no discount is given, then what will be the profit percentage?
e_en: Given: 30 percent of marked price is equal to 50 percent of cost price Formula used: Profit % = (Selling Price - Cost Price)/Cost Price × 100 Solution: ⇒ From the given data, derive the relation between marked price and cost price ⇒ Selling Price = Marked Price (since no discount is given) MP × 30/100 = CP × 50/100 ⇒ MP/CP = 5/3 So SP = 5 Profit% = [(5 - 3)/3] × 100 = 66.67% Therefore, the profit percentage when no discount is given is 66.67 percent (option A).

q_en: Find the compound interest (CI) on Rs. 12,600 for 2 years at 10% per annum compounded annually.
e_en: Given: Principal (P) = Rs. 12,600 Rate (R) = 10% Time (T) = 2 years Concept used: Compound Interest formula Solution: ⇒ CI = P(1 + R/100)² - P ⇒ CI = 12600(1 + 10/100)² - 12600 ⇒ CI = 15246 - 12600 = 2646 Therefore, the compound interest on Rs. 12,600 for 2 years at 10% per annum compounded annually is Rs. 2646

q_en: Rohit buys an old bat for Rs. 880 and spends Rs. 120 on its repairing. If he sells it for Rs. 800, then what is the loss percentage?
e_en: Given: Cost of old bat = Rs. 880 Repairing cost = Rs. 120 Selling price = Rs. 800 Concept: Loss% = (Loss/CP) × 100% Solution: ⇒ CP = Cost of old bat + Repairing cost = 880 + 120 = Rs. 1000 ⇒ Loss = CP - Selling price = 1000 - 800 = Rs. 200 ⇒ Loss% = (200/1000) × 100% = 20% Therefore, the loss percentage is 20%.

q_en: The third proportional to 4 and 6 is:

q_en: A wire is in the form of square with side 44 cm. It is bent to form a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
e_en: Given: Side of the square = 44 cm Formula used: Perimeter of the square = 4 × side = 4 × 44 = 176 cm (which is the circumference of the circle) Radius of the circle = Circumference/(2π) Calculation: Radius = 176 / (2π) ⇒ Radius = 28 cm Therefore, the radius of the circle is 28 cm.

q_en: A mixture contains milk and water in the ratio 5 ∶ 2. If 4 liters of water is added to the mixture, the ratio becomes 5 ∶ 4. What is the quantity of milk in the given mixture?
e_en: Given: Original ratio of milk and water = 5 ∶ 2, New ratio after adding 4 liters of water = 5 ∶ 4 Concept used: Quantity of milk stays the same, so water must have increased from 2 parts to 4 parts Calculation: Quantity of milk = (5/2) × 4 ⇒ Quantity of milk = 10 liters Therefore, the quantity of milk in the mixture is 10 liters.

q_en: What is the single equivalent price increase for two successive price increase of 5% and 8% on an item?
e_en: Given: First increase = 5% = 0.05, Second increase = 8% = 0.08 Formula: Total increase = first increase + second increase + (first increase × second increase) Calculation: Total increase = 0.05 + 0.08 + (0.05 × 0.08) ⇒ Total increase ≈ 0.134 or 13.4% Therefore, the single equivalent price increase is 13.4%.

q_en: A person walks 10 km at a speed of 2.5 km per hour, then runs 10 km at a speed of 5 km per hour and then goes 30 km by bus at the speed of 30 km per hour. What is the average speed of the man?
e_en: Given: Distance walked = 10 km, Speed while walking = 2.5 km/h, Distance run = 10 km, Speed while running = 5 km/h, Distance by bus = 30 km, Speed by bus = 30 km/h Formula used: Average speed = Total distance / Total time Calculation: Total distance = 10 + 10 + 30 ⇒ Total distance = 50 km Total time = (10/2.5) + (10/5) + (30/30) = 7 hours Average speed = 50/7 ≈ 7.14 km/h Hence, the average speed of the man is 7.14 km/h.

q_en: Rohan alone can do a work in 10 days and Mohan alone can do the same work in 15 days. In how many days will they together complete the same work?
e_en: Given: Rohan's time = 10 days, Mohan's time = 15 days Formula used: 1/Rohan's time + 1/Mohan's time = 1/Total time Calculation: 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/Total time ⇒ Total time = 30/(5) ⇒ 6 days Hence, they will complete the work together in 6 days.

q_en: What is the effective annual rate of interest corresponding to a nominal rate of 10% per annum payable half-yearly?
e_en: Given: Nominal interest rate = 10% per annum, Number of compounding periods = 2 Formula used: Effective annual rate = (1 + r/n)⁽ⁿt⁾ - 1, where r is the nominal rate, n is the number of compounding periods, and t is the time in years. Calculation: Effective annual rate = (1 + 0.1/2)⁽² × ¹⁾ - 1 ⇒ Effective annual rate ≈ 0.1025 or 10.25% Therefore, the effective annual rate of interest is 10.25%.

q_en: A person bought some pens at the rate of 30 for a rupee and sold them at the rate of 20 for a rupee. What is the profit percentage?
e_en: Given: Cost price for 30 pens = Rs. 1, Selling price for 20 pens = Rs. 1 Formula used: Profit = Selling Price - Cost Price Profit percentage = (Profit/Cost price) × 100 Calculation: Profit = (1/20) - (1/30) ⇒ Profit = 0.05 - 0.03333 ⇒ Profit = 0.01667 per pen Profit percentage = (Profit/Cost price) × 100 ⇒ Profit percentage = (0.01667 / 0.03333) × 100 ≈ 50% Hence, the profit percentage is 50%.

q_en: X, Y and Z enter into a partnership. X invests some money at the beginning. Y Invests thrice the amount of X after 4 months and Z invest double the amount of Y after 9 months from the beginning. If the annual gain be Rs. 450000, then what is the share of Y?

q_en: A water purifier is on sale for 10% discount on the original price. A store- wide sale results in an additional discount of 15%. What is the total discount on the original price?

e_en: Given Data: Man paints in 9 days Woman paints in 18 days 3 men and 3 women Concept: Use the concept of combined work rate. Solution: Man = 9 Women = 18 LCM = 18 Unit work by man = 2 Unit work by women = 1 Total work done by 3 men and 3 women = 3 × 2 + 3 × 1 = 9 Work done = 18/9 = 2 days. Therefore, they will paint the house in 2 days.

q_en: A truck covers a distance of 540 km at a certain speed in 9 hours. How much time would a car take at an average speed which is 16 km/hr more than that of the speed of the truck to cover a distance which is 68 km more than that travelled by the truck?
e_en: Given Data: Truck distance: 540 km in 9 hours Car distance: 68 km more, speed 16 km/hr more Concept: Calculate the time using the formula Time = (Distance)/(Speed) Solution: ⇒ Truck speed = 540/9=60 km/hr ⇒ Car speed = 60 + 16 = 76 km/hr ⇒ Car distance = 540 + 68 = 608 km ⇒ Car time = 608/76=8 hours Therefore, the car would take 8 hours.

q_en: The average of five consecutive odd numbers is 37. What is the sum of the highest and the lowest number?
e_en: Given Data: Average of five consecutive odd numbers: 37 Concept: Use the fact that consecutive odd numbers have a difference of 2 and the mean is the middle value. Solution: Since the average is 37, so middle number out of 5 is equal to the average. So, the third number is 37. ⇒ The five numbers are: 33, 35, 37, 39, 41 ⇒ Sum of highest and lowest = 33 + 41 = 74 Therefore, the sum of the highest and the lowest number is 74.

q_en: The marked price of an article is 160 percent of the cost price. If 20 percent discount is given, then what will be the profit percentage?
e_en: Given: Marked Price (MP) = 160% of Cost Price (CP) Discount = 20% of MP Find Profit Percentage Concept: Profit or Loss is calculated on CP. Solution: Let the CP = 100 (For simplicity) Hence, MP = 160 (As MP is 160% of CP) Discount = 20% of MP = 20% of 160 = 32 Selling Price (SP) = MP - Discount = 160 - 32 = 128 Profit = SP - CP = 128 - 100 = 28 Profit Percentage = (Profit/CP) × 100 = (28/100) × 100 = 28% Hence, the profit percentage is 28% (Option A).
